attributes.residual: Two mechanisms, both named, neither closed. (1) THE SWITCH, +0x134..+0x14c: source-unreachable and flag-unreachable, see the denial block. It is the ENTIRE count asymmetry -- the chain costs us 12 instructions where the table costs the target 6, plus the target's 2-instruction `lis`/`addi` table-base load, netting our +6. Because T275/O281 is count-asymmetric it is also outside every postprocessor class per claim.law.webfrank-cannot-close-instruction-count-deltas. (2) THE ENTRY-ADDRESS WEB, four `add`+`lwz` vs `addi`+`lwzx` sites plus one target-only `lwzu`: source-reachable and measurably real-improving, but fuzzy-negative in both forms tried; written out above for the next lane. A third, smaller observation: the frame is 8 bytes wider than target (32 vs 40) and probe 3 proved the two obvious dead locals are not the cause.

denial.falsifier: A compiler build outside the current build/compilers archive that emits a table at 5 distinct destinations, or a reading of jumptable_8011892C showing a 6th distinct destination that our reconstruction collapsed.
denial.premise_measurement: The switch needs a 6th distinct branch destination to emit a table (claim.law.AT_mwcc-emits-a-switch-jumptable-iff-six-distinct-branch-destinations.20260902.v1) and has 5: case 0 body, case 9 body, the shared case 1|2 body, the case 4 body, and the default. The retail table jumptable_8011892C (config/GUNE5D/symbols.txt: .data:0x8011892C, size 0x28) holds 10 entries resolving to those SAME 5 addresses (+0x14C, +0x180 x2, +0x1D0 x5, +0x1B0, +0x16C), so our case set already equals the target's and adding a destination would be inventing semantics the target does not have. Harness: 12/12 shapes agree with the rule, 0/17 flag settings and 0/29 archive compilers emit a table for this shape.
denial.scope: One axis on one function: closing init_attract_mode's first switch (the `(u32)(lbl_80344290 - 0x8000)` dispatch at +0x134..+0x14c) by any SOURCE-LEVEL rewriting of its cases -- labels, order, grouping, `default:` placement, cast signedness, empty-group spelling -- or by any per-TU optimization flag or pragma. Does NOT deny work on the function's other clusters, and does NOT deny the postprocessor path on grounds other than the count asymmetry.

hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes -- read at fnasm game/ui/attract.c init_attract_mode 0xe8:0x120 --diff and 0x110:0x180 --diff. The target's r31 is the raw lbl_80118188 base and r8 the recomputed element pointer; the target repeats `add` before each field touch rather than caching, which is exactly the cached-base law's target-side fingerprint.
hypothesis.statement: The remaining, still-open half of this function is the ENTRY-ADDRESS WEB, not the switch. The target holds base+cur*8 in a register and reaches fields at a displacement (`add r8,r31,r6` then `lwz r6,16(r8)`, plus a walked `lwzu`), where we fold the +16 into the index and emit `addi`+`lwzx` at four sites. Removing the cached `entry` alias per claim.law.cached-base-alias-defeats-rematerialized-index-base moves real 202->199 and, with the two dead locals also dropped, 202->189 with the count going 281->280 -- but BOTH states regress fresh objdiff fuzzy (-0.1345 and -0.1164). A lane that can explain WHY fuzzy falls while real, instruction count and the opcode multiset all improve should re-run these two forms; they are written out verbatim below and neither was banked.
